content.appVersions: Below the minimum version of its app: a full screen 'Uppdatera appen' / 'Mettre à jour l'app' / 'Update the app' with a store button; the app is blocked. Below the recommended version: a message the user can close. During a trip (rider on board, or driver on a trip) only a small message: the block starts after the trip ends. SOS always works.
content.legal: When a legal item is published with reaccept true: the next time the app opens (never during a trip) it shows the new terms with 'Jag godkänner' / 'J'accepte' / 'I accept'; POST /account/terms/accept { contentVersion } stores who accepted and when (GET /admin/content/legal/acceptances?zoneId lists them). Until accepted, the rider cannot book and the driver cannot go online.

zones.note: v0.11.0 (owner 2026-10-28 and decision #9 'the server's list is the truth; the admin reads it and creates zones on the server'): the zones live on the server. The admin's Zones page reads, creates, edits (outline drawn on the map) and opens or closes them; the apps read the open zones with their outline and names.
zones.zone: Zone { zoneId, names: { sv, fr, en }, country (ISO 3166 alpha-2), currency (SEK | EUR | TND), timeZone (IANA), kind: operating | airport, polygon: [[lat, lng], ...], bounds: { south, west, north, east }, center: { lat, lng }, open, version, createdAt, updatedAt, updatedBy? }
zones.idScheme: Ids are fixed at creation and never change (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$). Existing ids stay (Stockholm Z001-Z009). A new city zone is <country>-<two capital letters> (FR-PC Paris & Ile-de-France, TN-TC Grand Tunis, the ids the apps already use); an airport zone is the IATA code (ARN, BMA, CDG, ORY).
zones.polygon: The outline as the admin draws it: 3 to 500 points [lat, lng] (lat -90..90, lng -180..180), in order, not closed (the last point is not the first again), not self-crossing. The server computes bounds (the polygon's bounding rectangle) and, on create and on a new outline, center (the middle of bounds); both are ignored in a request. A point on the edge is inside.
zones.names: names.sv, names.fr and names.en are all required (1-80 characters). The apps show the name in the app language.
zones.neverDeleted: A zone is never deleted, only closed. There is no DELETE; trips, documents and history keep their zoneId.
zones.open: POST /admin/zones/{zoneId}/open and /close (zones.edit) set open; an open zone takes new rides, a closed one does not (rides already booked go on). Both send expectedVersion and raise version.
zones.permissions: GET /admin/zones: zones.read, the zones in the admin's scope (a Super admin: all). POST, PUT, open, close: zones.edit, one admin is enough (no second admin), written in the audit (zone.create, zone.update, zone.open, zone.close). An admin may change a zone in its scope; creating one needs the whole scope (*) or a zone of the same country in scope (403 forbidden zone_out_of_scope otherwise).
zones.version: Zone.version starts at 1 and goes up by one with every change; PUT, open and close send expectedVersion (409 version_mismatch with the current zone otherwise). country, currency and timeZone cannot change after creation (400 invalid_request zone_field_fixed).
zones.lookup: The zone of a point: among zones whose bounds hold it, those whose polygon holds it; an open zone before a closed one, then a city (operating) zone before an airport, then the smallest bounds. An airport zone inside a city zone (ARN in Z001, CDG and ORY in FR-PC) does not take the ride; it adds the airport fees (contract.json#pricing.requestExtras.airport), whether open or not.
zones.notHere: A quote or booking whose pickup lies in no OPEN zone is 403 forbidden, reason service_not_available (the server's existing code). The rider app then shows 'Movera isn't here yet' (sv 'Movera finns inte här än', fr 'Movera n’est pas encore ici') and cannot book; it may check GET /rider/zones first.
zones.apps: GET /rider/zones and GET /driver/zones (?country=FR optional) → { zones: Zone[] }: the OPEN zones (of that country, else all), with polygon and names; closed zones are never listed. The apps read them on start and on config_published with doc zones.
zones.notify: Every create, update, open and close sends config_published { doc: 'zones', zoneId, version, publishedAt }. It arrives on the rider and driver config streams (GET /rider/config/stream, /driver/config/stream) whatever zone they follow; a content publish (doc 'content') arrives on the streams of its zone. Their SSE id stays the app document's version.

statusWords.note: v0.10.4 (owner 2026-10-28): ONE STATUS WORD LIST. The words the admin, rider and driver apps show for every status code, per family, in sv, fr and en. Swedish agrees with the noun of the family (documents, vehicles, offers, ratings, tickets, incidents are neuter: Godkänt, Utgånget, Avslaget). The rider is "Resenär" in Swedish, never "Passagerare". An app shows these words, never its own; a code without a word is a contract error (reference_check.py).

chat.note: v0.13.0 (CONTRACT.md §23, owner decisions 2026-10-28 and 'chat only support roles in their zones'): trip chat between the trip's rider and driver, read and written by support admins of the trip's zone; calls go through a masked number; no phone numbers in rider or driver payloads.
chat.adminScope: An admin reads (GET) and writes (POST) /trips/{tripId}/messages only with support.reply and only for a trip in one of the admin's zones (super admin: all). Without the permission: 403 forbidden; outside the zones: 403 forbidden, reason zone_out_of_scope.
chat.window: The chat is open from driver assignment until drop-off. When the trip is terminal (tripStatus.terminal) a POST from the rider or the driver is 409 invalid_transition, reason chat_closed; there is no grace period after the trip (the earlier 1 hour is removed). v0.18.5: after the trip the rider and the driver read no history (chat.appStorage.afterTrip); admins read it while the messages are kept. Support (admin) may still write on a closed trip.
chat.retention: A daily server job deletes trip chat messages older than 90 days. Messages of a trip that has a safety incident (SOS, driver_silent or any incident linked to the trip) are kept with the case and are deleted only with the case.
chat.fleetChat: None: there is no fleet owner to driver chat.
chat.noPhoneNumbers: Rider and driver payloads (TripProjection rider/driver views, Message, realtime envelopes, SupportTicket in the apps) never carry the other side's real phone number. Only the person's own profile carries their own phone.

call.who: The trip's rider or driver, while the trip is in chat.openStatuses.
call.answer: 200 TripCall { tripId, proxyNumber, expiresAt }: dial proxyNumber; the telephony provider bridges to the other side without showing either real number.
call.unavailable: 503 unavailable, reason call_unavailable, while no telephony provider is set up (the server default). The app then hides the call button or offers the chat.
call.closed: 409 invalid_transition, reason chat_closed, outside the open statuses.
call.provider: Number masking needs a telephony provider. The owner must pick one; the server reads its keys from the environment, never from git. Until then the provider is 'disabled'.

appStorage.note: v0.18.5 (owner 2026-10-30: "Never store messages between rider or driver in driver app or rider app !!!!!!' Only admin panel inside the ride details"): the chat between rider and driver lives only during the trip.
appStorage.noBellNotice: The server writes no stored notification (GET /notifications) for a chat message, so no bell line carries a message. Notices kind trip_message already stored are deleted (server migration).
appStorage.liveAlert: While the trip is open the other side learns of a message only through the trip stream (event kind message); the app may show a short 'New message' alert and play a sound, without the text and without keeping it.
appStorage.afterTrip: Once the trip is terminal, GET /trips/{tripId}/messages answers { items: [], nextCursor: null, closed: true } to the rider and the driver, and their trip events (GET /trips/{tripId}/events and the stream) carry no message text. The apps clear the chat when the trip ends and keep no copy.
appStorage.admin: Admins with support.reply keep the full chat in the trip details (GET /trips/{tripId}/messages as admin), within chat.retentionDays.

tripPath.note: v0.17.0 (owner 2026-10-29, driver past ride detail; CONTRACT.md §25): the route of an ended trip for the trip's own driver or rider, drawn on the past-ride map with pickup and drop-off pins.
tripPath.path: GET /trips/{tripId}/path → TripPath { tripId, source: driven | planned, points: LatLng[], pickup, dropoff, stops, keptUntil? }
tripPath.actors: the trip's rider or the trip's driver (anyone else: 404 not_found, like GET /trips/{tripId}); only once the trip is terminal (tripStatus.terminal), else 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_ended
tripPath.driven: The driven path is made from the trip's own GPS trace (the fixes of POST /driver/location kept in the trip trace, §12) from boarding to the end: fixes with accuracy ≤ 50 m, a step only once the car moved 25 m, no step faster than 150 km/h, then evenly thinned to at most maxPoints. At least 2 such points are needed.
tripPath.planned: No usable trace (the trace was deleted after liveDrivers.traceKeepDays, or never sent): the server's road route (§10, OSRM or the straight-line estimate) from the pickup through the stops to the drop-off.
tripPath.retention: No new storage: the driven path is read from the trip trace and follows its rule (deleted traceKeepDays = 30 days after the fix); afterwards the answer is the planned route. keptUntil is when the trace goes.
tripPath.apps: The driver's past-ride screen (and the rider's, when it reads the server) shows the line and pins; a failed call shows the pickup and drop-off pins only.

completePreview.note: v0.18.1 (owner 2026-10-29, live bug A, 'Server's final price (Recommended)'; CONTRACT.md §26): the driver app asks the server for the final price before it shows Collect cash, so the driver, the rider, the receipt and the history all show the same amount.
completePreview.path: GET /driver/trips/{tripId}/complete-preview → CompletePreview { previewId, expiresAt, tripId, total: Money, cashDue: Money, driverEarnings: Money, earlyEnd: boolean, fareLines: FareLine[] }
completePreview.actors: the trip's own driver (anyone else 404 not_found); only while the trip is on board (rider_onboard, in_trip, approaching_dropoff), else 409 invalid_transition, reason trip_not_on_board. No Idempotency-Key; the wallet is not touched; the trip's version does not change. Each call freezes its price for freezeSeconds and replaces the trip's earlier preview.
completePreview.same: total and fareLines are computed by the same code as POST /trips/{tripId}/complete would at that moment with the driver's latest fix (pricing.driverEndsEarly): earlyEnd is true when the driver is farther than pricing.completeNearDropoffMeters from the drop-off. cashDue = total − the part the rider's wallet would pay. driverEarnings = the driver's part of that total (as TripProjection.driverEarnings after complete), for the sheet's cash balance.
completePreview.cashCollected: The app sends POST /trips/{tripId}/complete { expectedVersion, previewId, cashCollected = the cashDue it showed } on a cash trip. On 409 price_changed it shows the sheet again with error.preview (never resends the old amount). After completing the app shows the fare of the returned TripProjection. An older server without the preview (404) leaves the app on the old flow (complete without cashCollected).
completePreview.apps: Collect <cashDue>; when earlyEnd also 'Ending before the destination – price recalculated' (sv: 'Avslutas före destinationen – priset räknades om', fr: 'Fin avant la destination – prix recalculé'). If the preview fails the app does not show a booked price as the amount to collect. The sheet's earnings line is the driver's own earnings from the preview (driverEarnings), labelled 'Your earnings' / 'Din intäkt' / 'Vos gains'.
completePreview.frozen: POST /trips/{tripId}/complete { expectedVersion, previewId, cashCollected } with the trip's latest previewId before expiresAt: complete uses the frozen price exactly (total, fareLines, driverEarnings, earlyEnd): no early-end flip, no extra minutes or waiting. On a cash trip cashCollected must equal its cashDue (and the wallet part must be unchanged); otherwise 409 conflict, reason price_changed, with a fresh preview in the error's preview field.
completePreview.unfrozen: previewId missing, unknown or expired: complete prices the trip as now. If the app sent previewId with cashCollected and that no longer equals the cash part of the new price: 409 conflict, reason price_changed, with a fresh preview (error.preview); the trip is not completed and the driver is never trapped by a 400. Without previewId (older apps) cashCollected keeps its old rule (at most the fare less the wallet, else 400 cash_above_fare).
completePreview.stored: A completed trip's cashCollected is always the cash part of its final fare when a previewId was sent.

The server also sends the set_offline bell + push notice with data { reason, note?, minutes? (no_position), count? (missed_offers) } for every server reason; its body is the reason text (no_position keeps 'Tap to go online again'). Paths: the no-position job (no_position), auto-offline after missed offers (missed_offers), car review rejected / blocked (vehicle_blocked), removed from the fleet or fleet blocked (fleet_removed), account status not active (account_status), and the end of a trip when the driver, car or fleet was blocked during it (account_status / vehicle_blocked / fleet_removed). A driver who leaves his fleet himself or starts his own company gets no reason (his own action). app_restart is set by the app only. Outside his area never sets a driver offline. The driver app's offline card shows reasons[offlineReason] in sv / fr / en.

outsideArea.note: G3-R2. A driver may go online anywhere (POST /driver/availability online is 200 even outside his zones), but he gets trips only while his latest position is inside one of his own zones (Driver.zoneIds): dispatch offers nothing to an online driver whose latest fix is outside all of them, and offers only trips of his own zones (as before). Driver (GET /driver/profile and the POST /driver/availability answer) and DriverLocationAck (POST /driver/location) carry outsideArea (true/false, missing while the server has no position) and, when true, areaZones (the driver's own zones with their names). The driver app shows the popup when outsideArea turns true (on going online and when he drives out), not again until it was false. Admin direct assign is the admin's choice and is not limited.

driverHome.scheduledRidesPerDriver: G3-R3 (owner 2026-10-30 'Remove the switch'): the admin's per-driver 'Scheduled driver access' switch is removed; every driver can take booked rides (the zone's reservations.on still decides). No server path ever set Driver.scheduledRides; the field (owner decision 2, v0.4.2) stays in the schema for older apps and is never sent; apps ignore it.

ridersOnline.note: G3-R4 (owner 'Real numbers only'): riders online per zone = distinct riders who in the last windowSeconds called GET /rider/nearby-vehicles (the open rider map) or POST /quotes (zone of the map point / pickup), plus riders with an open request (trip requested, searching or offered) in that zone. Served on GET /admin/live/drivers as LiveDriverList.ridersOnline [{ zoneId, count }] (the admin's zones only, zones with 0 included) — the admin Dashboard's 'Riders online' shows it; no invented numbers.

performance.note: G3-D2 (owner 2026-10-30, 'Real numbers'). The server computes the driver's own numbers over the last windowDays days (rolling, server clock) and sends them as Driver.performance on GET /driver/profile (the driver himself) and GET /admin/drivers/{driverId} (admin). Same counts as the dispatch score inputs (CONTRACT.md §3.6 factors acceptance and cancel): offersAnswerable = the driver's offers of kind exclusive or assigned sent in the window that ended claimed, declined or expired (withdrawn and claimed_elsewhere are not counted: he could not answer them); offersAccepted = those claimed; acceptancePct = round(offersAccepted / offersAnswerable × 100); tripsCancelled = the driver's cancels after accepting (driver_cancels) in the window; cancellationPct = round(min(100, tripsCancelled / offersAccepted × 100)). acceptancePct is null while offersAnswerable < minOffers; cancellationPct is null while offersAccepted < minTrips. rating = the average of the riders' visible ratings (hidden ratings not counted, 2 decimals), null while ratingCount < minRatings. The app shows '—' for null (sv/fr/en: same dash). Dispatch (§3.6) uses these same counts unrounded as soon as there is any data (the minimums only decide what the apps show); with no data at all it uses the §3.6 defaults (rating 4.7, acceptance 85 %, cancels 5 %).

nearbyBlur.note: G3-D4 (owner 2026-10-30, 'Slightly moved'). GET /rider/nearby-vehicles never gives a driver's exact position: each car is moved by an offset of minMeters..maxMeters in a direction, both taken from an HMAC of the driver id and the time slot of stableMinutes (server clock), so a car does not jump between answers inside a slot; the offset changes at the next slot. The answer still carries no identity (opaque key, contract.json#riderNearby). The exact position is shown only to the rider of a trip a driver accepted, through the existing trip views (TripProjection driver location).

zoneSupply.note: G3-D5 (owner 2026-10-30, 'Fix it'). LiveDriverList.zoneSupply on GET /admin/live/drivers: one row per zone of the answer, the Dashboard's supply/demand rows AND its shortage alert use these same numbers. Every driver online or on_trip counts in his zone (LiveDriver.zoneId: the zone of his latest position, else his first own zone), stale position included. online = those drivers; free = online drivers with onlineStatus online and no active trip; busy = online − free; waiting = trips of the zone in status requested, searching or offered with no driver yet (live rides only, not reservations before their search starts). level: ok when waiting = 0; tight when 0 < waiting <= free; short when waiting > free. shortage = level short. The panel shows the shortage alert only when at least one row has shortage true and names those rows.

legal.note: v0.18.5 (owner G1-B2 "Real texts from admin (Recommended)"): the terms of use and the privacy policy per country (SE, FR) in sv / fr / en, edited by the admin (Content › Legal, the content place legal), versioned, shown in both apps (also before sign-in) and accepted again when a new version asks for it. The built-in texts are Movera-made drafts: a lawyer must review them before launch.
legal.lawyerReview: Drafts (version 0) say so on their first line. A lawyer reviews the texts before launch; the admin publishes the reviewed ones.
legal.company: LegalCompany { companyName?, orgNumber?, address?, supportEmail?, supportPhone? }, filled by the admin. In the texts a placeholder {companyName} … is replaced by the admin's value; a paragraph whose placeholder has no value is left out, so nothing empty or made up is shown.
legal.read: GET /legal/{country} (no token, auth.beforeSignIn.allowed) → LegalTexts { country, version, source: default | admin, publishedAt?, reaccept, reacceptFrom, terms: LegalDocument { title, text } , privacy: LegalDocument } with title and text in sv / fr / en and the placeholders already filled. version 0 = the built-in drafts (nothing published). Unknown country: 404 not_found (reason legal_country_unknown). Apps read it on start and when they come back to the foreground (no stream event), and keep the last answer offline. reacceptFrom = the newest version published with reaccept true (null when none was): the version a person must have accepted (or a later one). v0.18.8: ?zoneId= (optional) fills {waitingRules} with that zone's live waiting, no-show and cancel numbers (contract.json#arrivedWaiting.termsTexts).
legal.admin: GET /admin/legal/{country} (settings.read) → LegalAdminView { live: LegalVersion (raw texts with placeholders and company), history: LegalVersion[] newest first }; POST /admin/legal/{country}/publish { terms: { title, text }, privacy: { title, text }, company?, reaccept? } (settings.publish, audited legal.publish) → LegalVersion with version + 1; every title and text needs sv, fr and en (text up to 20000 characters). An admin with a zone in that country, or a Super admin, may edit it.
legal.accept: POST /account/legal/accept { country, version } (rider, driver) → 204; version must be the live one (409 conflict, reason terms_version_not_current). Who must accept: the newest version published with reaccept true (LegalTexts.reacceptFrom) is the one that counts; accepting it or any later version satisfies it (accepting v3 also satisfies v2), and a later publish without reaccept never unblocks a person who did not accept it. Until then the rider cannot book (POST /trips 409 conflict, reason terms_not_accepted) and the driver cannot go online (POST /driver/availability 409 invalid_transition, reason terms_not_accepted); a person counts for the countries of his zones (rider: the pickup zone; driver: his zones and his latest position's zone). Version 0 needs no accept (accepted at sign-up).
legal.apps: Both apps show 'Terms' and 'Privacy' as two separate links on the sign-in screen and in the menu, read from GET /legal/{country} of the start country (auth.startCountry), else of the account's country. When reacceptFrom is not null and the person has not accepted a version >= reacceptFrom (it then accepts the live version), the next app start (never during a trip) shows the new terms with 'Jag godkänner' / 'J'accepte' / 'I accept'.
legal.legacyContent: The zone content item legal (§19) stays readable for older apps; new apps use GET /legal/{country}.

text.sv:
Utkast – granskas av jurist före lansering.

1. Tjänsten. Movera förmedlar resor mellan passagerare och förare med taxitrafiktillstånd i Sverige. Resan utförs av föraren och dess åkeri.

2. Konto. Du registrerar dig med ditt mobilnummer och ansvarar för att uppgifterna är riktiga. Du måste vara minst 18 år.

driverOffers.note: v0.18.6 (owner decisions 1–7 of 2026-10-29 and answers G4-E1..E7 of 2026-10-30, driver group 4 'Incoming offer & exclusive offer', Rules decisions/driver-g4.md). Works the same in every country (SE and FR); every text in sv / fr / en.

push.note: Decision 1 + E6. For every new offer (feed event offer_created) the server also sends a push to the driver's registered fcm devices (auth.devices.sending: after the command commits, one retry, dead tokens removed), so a driver whose app is in the background or whose phone is locked hears and sees it. It is NOT a bell notice: it never appears in GET /notifications, is not counted unread and cannot be marked read (404). A push not handed to Firebase before the offer's expiresAt is dropped. Title and body in the driver's account language (else the zone's default). The app in the foreground ignores the push (the offer stream already shows the offer). A tap opens the app at data.deepLink: the offer card while the offer is still open, else Home.
push.rule: E6 (owner 'Sound + vibration'): Exclusive and hand-sent (assigned) offers play the Movera offer sound and vibrate (vibration only while the driver's own Vibrate setting in the app is on), in the foreground and in the push; Radar offers stay quiet (no sound, no vibration).

data.expiresAt: Offer.expiresAt (ISO time); the app shows nothing after it

native.note: Android: an offer with sound uses the notification channel androidChannel (sound file soundFile, vibration on, high importance); a quiet one androidQuietChannel (no sound, no vibration). iOS: aps.sound iosSound, none when quiet; interruption-level time-sensitive. Web: data-only message; the service worker shows it (silent when quiet; vibrate webVibratePattern when vibrate is 'true') and the open page plays the sound. The native apps add the sound file and the two channels when their store builds are made.

riderRating.note: Decision 3 (owner 'Show it'): Offer.riderRating = the rider's average of the visible ratings drivers gave him (riders' own rating, as Rider.rating), rounded to 2 decimals; the card shows it with one decimal and a star. Shown by default. A rider with no rating yet gets NO riderRating (the card shows nothing; never a made-up value — the old 4.9 fallback idea is dropped). The admin turns it off per zone with DriverAppConfig.offers.offerCard.riderRating = false (Settings › Driver app › Offer card, per zone or the country standard): the server then sends no riderRating on offers of trips in that zone, and the app also hides it. The value is taken when the offer is sent and does not change on that offer.

acceptCheck.note: Decision 4 (owner 'Lock + Accepting… + check'). The app locks the Accept button at the first tap and shows texts.accepting. It sends POST /offers/{offerId}/accept with an Idempotency-Key. When the answer is lost (network error, no answer within answerTimeoutSeconds), it asks the server GET /driver/offers/{offerId} → OfferCheck { offer, trip? } (every checkEverySeconds, until checkForSeconds): offer.status claimed and trip present → open that trip (it is his); offer.status open and expiresAt not passed → send the SAME accept again with the SAME Idempotency-Key (the server answers the first result if it already ran); any other status (claimed_elsewhere, expired, withdrawn, declined) → texts.gone for 2 s on the island at the top of Home (decision 5; it is not a miss). Only the offer's own driver may read it (another driver's offer is 404 offer_not_found).

driverOffers.whyYouRemoved: E7 (owner 'Remove short line explain'): the 'why you got this trip' line is removed from the offer card. The server no longer sends Offer.reasonCode (deprecated, kept in the schema so older builds keep working: they show no line when it is missing) and DriverAppConfig.offers.exclusiveReasons is deprecated and ignored (apps never show it; the admin hides its Dispatch › Exclusive reasons editor). It was only used on the offer card.
driverOffers.declinedComesBack: E1 (owner 'Can come back later'): no change. An Exclusive offer the driver declined or missed may come back to him later as a Radar offer if nobody else took the trip.
driverOffers.notDecided: E5 (rider 'Keep waiting?' steps vs the rider app's own 3-minute card) is NOT decided (owner: ask again later); the rider-waiting steps are unchanged in v0.18.6.

dispatchTools.note: v0.18.6 (owner decisions G4-F1..F6 of 2026-10-31, Rules decisions/driver-g4.md, research plan/g4-admin-features.md): the admin's Dispatch tools, real on the server. Everything is per country (SE, FR): an admin reads and changes a country's items only with a zone of that country in scope (Super admin: all), else 403 zone_out_of_scope. Writes need dispatch.edit, reads trips.read; every write is audited (auditActions) and takes an Idempotency-Key. Each item has a version: PUT and DELETE need expectedVersion (409 version_mismatch with the item). Names: 1–40 characters, unique per country (409 conflict, reason name_taken).
dispatchTools.approvals: F1 (owner 'Live now, remove box'): dispatch changes (publishing the dispatch document, the zone's dispatch switch, presets, groups, radar zones, rules, events, sends) never wait for a second admin: the one-admin rule of 2026-10-28 (adminControlMatrix.oneAdmin) stays. The panel removes the 'Waiting for a second admin' box and badge; History + Undo stay. Dispatch approvals still pending from before that rule were expired by server migration 0040.

presets.note: F2 (owner 'Per country only'): saved Dispatch presets per country. values = a DispatchDocument without version, publishedAt, zoneId, country, timeZone and usesStandard (checked like the document; 400 invalid_document). Any admin with dispatch.edit may save, rename, change or delete one. Applying a preset is the panel's job: it copies values into the zone's dispatch draft (PUT /admin/config/dispatch) and publishes as usual.

groups.note: F3 (owner 'Free ones, nearest first'): driver groups per country, admin only (drivers are never told). Every driver must be of the group's country (400 invalid_request, reason driver_not_in_country); at most 200 drivers. Send to a group: POST /admin/trips/{tripId}/radar-group { expectedVersion, groupId } — the server picks the group's FREE members (account active, online, not on a trip, a position newer than 120 s, the trip's category, no open offer for this trip), nearest to the pickup first, at most 10, and sends them a radar offer each (as a radar group). A member who is not free is skipped, never an error; 409 conflict, reason no_free_driver, only when no member is free. Reservations will use groups with group 15 (a group used by a reservation rule will then be 409 group_in_use on delete; nothing uses groups yet).
groups.entity: DriverGroup { groupId, country, name, driverIds, version, createdBy?, createdAt, updatedBy?, updatedAt }

radarZones.note: F4 (owner 'Repeat until taken'): radar zones (an area drawn inside one operating zone of the country; polygon as contract.json#zones.polygon, 3–500 points) and radar zone rules per country. A rule says which radar zones it is for ('all' or a list of radarZoneIds of its country), how long each send stays open (seconds 5–120), how many drivers at most (maxDrivers 1–10) and whether it sends again by itself (repeat). Manual admin sends only: automatic dispatch never uses radar zones. Send: POST /admin/trips/{tripId}/radar-group { expectedVersion, radarZoneId, ruleId } (the rule must cover the radar zone: 400 rule_not_for_zone) → radar offers to the free drivers (as for groups) whose latest position is inside the polygon, nearest to the pickup first, up to rule.maxDrivers, open rule.seconds. Without repeat: 409 no_free_driver when nobody is free inside. With repeat: when the offers run out and nobody accepted, the server sends again to whoever is free inside the area then (newcomers included; drivers who still hold an open offer of this trip are skipped), every rule.seconds, until a driver accepts, an admin stops it (POST /admin/trips/{tripId}/radar-zone/stop), the rider's search ends (8 min) or the trip ends; a round with nobody free inside waits for the next. A new radar-zone send on the same trip replaces the running one. GET /admin/dispatch/radar-zones/{radarZoneId}/free?categoryId= → { radarZoneId, free, at } counts the free drivers inside now. A radar zone used by a rule's list cannot be deleted (409 conflict, reason radar_zone_in_use).

routes: POST /admin/trips/{tripId}/radar-zone/stop { note? } → RadarZoneSend (404 radar_zone_send_not_found when none runs)

The send ends at once (not at the next interval) when a driver accepts (stopReason accepted), the trip is cancelled or ends (trip_over), the rider's search ends (search_ended), an admin stops it (admin) or a new radar-zone send replaces it (replaced).

debtByCurrency.note: Q3 (CRITICAL fix): an owed cash fee (cancel or no-show, CONTRACT.md §3.7) is charged again only on a trip in the SAME currency. A rider who owes 100 kr from Stockholm is quoted in Paris without it (never +100 €); the debt waits for the next Swedish trip. So a driver or rider in a French zone gets the French zone's terms in euro, a Swedish one the Swedish terms in kronor. It is TripProjection.eta (TripEta) on every read and rides on a kind=location event (etaSeconds + eta; no version change) on the trip stream, for the rider, the driver and the admin. Both apps show eta.etaSeconds (whole minutes rounded up, at least 1) and eta.distanceMeters as distanceDisplay says; neither app computes its own ETA for the trip screen (the driver's navigation app is a separate thing).

distanceDisplay.rule: meters ≥ 1000 → unit km, value floor(meters / 100) / 10 (one decimal); 100 ≤ meters < 1000 → unit m, value floor(meters / 100) × 100; meters < 100 → unit m, value max(10, floor(meters / 10) × 10)

The ETA tick comes on the stream every eta.everySeconds, so there is nothing to poll for. The driver app follows the same rule.

pickupMove.note: Status item 4 + note check (owner '200 m default, admin can change'): the rider moves the pickup with PATCH /trips/{tripId} { expectedVersion, pickup } while the trip is requested, searching, offered, accepted or driver_to_pickup. The server measures the straight-line distance from the BOOKED pickup (the first one) to the new one and refuses more than the zone's booking.maxPickupMoveMeters (the zone's driver document, admin Dispatch › Booking 'Pickup move after accept'; default 200, range 0–2000; server migration sets every published document still on the old 500 to 200): 400 invalid_request, reason pickup_move_too_far, details ["maxMeters=200", "meters=…"]. After the driver arrived: 409 invalid_transition, reason pickup_fixed_after_arrival. A move changes pickup, version + 1, and sends one event of kind pickup_moved (new realtime kind, with the projection, before terminal only) to the rider, the driver and the admin; the driver app re-routes and shows texts.island on the island; open offers show the new pickup on their next read; the fare does not change (≤ 200 m). The other UpdateTripRequest fields (dropoff, stops, routeQuoteId, payment method) are not served yet: 400 invalid_request, reason route_change_not_available (destination change is the next job, decision 5).

rules.source: DriverAppConfig.waiting (Admin › Dispatch › Waiting at pickup, per zone): farPickup { on, km, freeWaitMin, perMin, noShowAfterMin, noShowFee }, rideTypes { scheduled | airport | event: { on, freeWaitMin, perMin, noShowAfterMin, noShowFee, radiusMeters? (event), afterEndMin? (event) } } and stopFreeWaitMin (Admin › Zone › Stops 'Free wait at each stop'). A null field keeps the value it would have without the rule. Money fields are Money in the zone's currency; a Money in another currency is ignored (the category value stays). rideTypes.scheduled.freeWaitMin is the reservation policy's included waiting (the admin publishes it there). The rider document gets the same fields when served (GET /rider/config).
rules.base: The category's waiting terms from Pricing (pricingDocument.categories[categoryId].waiting: freeWaitMin, perMin, noShowAfterMin, noShowFee), as in v0.18.7.

match.airport: the trip's pickup lies in an airport zone (the server's price extra pickupInAirportZone, set at booking)
match.event: at arrive, an admin event (Dispatch › Events, the trip's country) is on and running (startsAt ≤ now ≤ endsAt + afterEndMin, default 0) and the pickup lies inside its polygon, or within radiusMeters (default 500) of its location when it has none
match.far_pickup: a live trip whose driver was more than farPickup.km away from the pickup when he accepted (Offer.pickupMeters of the accepted offer, strictly more than km × 1000)

rules.order: One ride type at most, the first that matches and is on: airport, then scheduled, then event. Then far_pickup on top. A later rule wins where it sets a value. When a rule sets freeWaitMin but not noShowAfterMin, noShowAfterMin follows it (owner decision 5: the no-show time is the end of the free waiting). Finally noShowAfterMin is never below freeWaitMin.
rules.appliedAt: arrive: the server computes the effective terms once, when the driver arrives, and keeps them on the trip (waiting.rules, freeWaitMin, perMin, noShowAfterMin, noShowFee; freeUntil / noShowAt from them). The waiting charge (board), the no-show fee, a cancel that counts as a no-show and the running total all use these numbers.
rules.snapshot: POST /trips keeps the zone's farPickup, rideTypes and stopFreeWaitMin of booking time (contract.json#bookingSnapshot field waitingRules); a later publish never changes a booked trip. A trip booked before v0.18.8 has none: no extra rule, no free stop minutes (as before).

projection.waiting: TripProjection.waiting gains (from arrive) rules: string[] (the applied rule ids, [] = the category's own terms), freeWaitMin, perMin: Money, noShowAfterMin (the effective numbers), paidMinutes (whole minutes of paid waiting, rounded up: from chargedSeconds once boarded, from chargedSecondsNow while arrived; for the admin waiting box — money is still counted by the second) and alerts (see alerts).
projection.terms: TripProjection.terms: from arrive, freeWaitMin, waitPerMin, noShowAfterMin and noShowFee are the effective numbers and terms.waitingRules lists the applied rule ids; before arrive they are the category's. New terms.stopFreeWaitMin (free minutes at each middle stop, 0 = none).

rules.stops: Free wait at each stop (owner re-check 2026-11-01): DriverAppConfig.waiting.stopFreeWaitMin (default 0 = no free minutes, as v0.7.1). stop_waiting charges, per stop, only the seconds after the first stopFreeWaitMin minutes of that stop (Σ max(0, (leftAt − arrivedAt) − stopFreeWaitMin × 60) / 60 × stopWaitPerMin).

pin.switch: DriverAppConfig.pickupPin { required: bool (default false), maxAttempts: int (default 5, 1–10), lockMinutes: int (default 5, 1–60) } — Admin › Zone › Safety 'Rider PIN before Start', per zone. Kept on the trip at booking (Trip.pinRequired); a later switch never changes a booked trip.
pin.code: With pinRequired the server makes a 4-digit PIN (0000–9999, random) when the trip is booked. The rider sees it: TripProjection.pickupPin (rider and admin views only; never the driver's, not on the driver's stream) and GET /trips/{tripId}/pin → PinCode { tripId, pin, expiresAt } (expiresAt = 24 h after booking or the booked time; once the trip is over 404 not_found, reason pin_trip_over). Without pinRequired: no pickupPin; GET /pin answers 404 not_found (reason pin_not_required).
pin.check: The driver sends the PIN: POST /trips/{tripId}/pin/verify { pin } → PinVerification { verifiedPinToken, expiresAt, version }, or directly { pin } in the body of board or start. Guesses are taken only while the trip is arrived (else 409 invalid_transition, reason pin_not_now). A trip with pinRequired cannot be boarded / started until the PIN was right once (TripProjection.pinVerified true): board / start without it → 409 invalid_transition (reason pin_required). A right PIN is its own change: version + 1 and a trip_projection event (the rider's pinVerified updates); with { pin } in board / start the step then goes on from that version (send the version you saw). Wrong PIN → 400 invalid_request (reason pin_wrong, details ['attemptsLeft=N']); after maxAttempts wrong tries in a row the trip is locked for lockMinutes → 429 rate_limited (reason pin_locked, retryAfterSeconds); after 3 × maxAttempts wrong tries in all the PIN is blocked → 429 rate_limited (reason pin_blocked, no retryAfterSeconds) until an admin unlocks it. Tries are counted although the command fails; the comparison is constant-time. verifiedPinToken is informative only (the verification is kept on the trip).
pin.admin: GET /admin/trips/{tripId} carries pickupPin, pinVerified, pinAttempts and pinBlocked (the admin can read the PIN to the driver on the phone). POST /admin/trips/{tripId}/pin/unlock { expectedVersion, reason } (trips.intervene, audited trip.pin_unlock) clears the lock, the block and the counts; the PIN stays.

Driver apps from 0.18.8 send the header X-Contract-Version (e.g. 0.18.8) on board / start; for a request without it, or with a lower version, the server skips the PIN check (and logs it), so an older app is never stuck. Only a trip with status no_show (else 409 invalid_transition, reason not_a_no_show).
reverseNoShow.effect: The status stays no_show (terminal statuses never change, §3) and the trip gets cancellation.reversal { at, by (adminId), reason, driverShareTakenBack }. The no-show fee goes: an owed fee is waived (feeStatus waived, Rider.outstanding recomputed); a fee already paid is refunded to the rider's wallet (wallet entry kind refund): feeStatus waived plus refundedAt and refundedToWallet true on cancellation (live 0.18.7 apps know only paid / owed / waived). The trip's fare becomes 0 (fareLines []). takeBackDriverShare false (default): the driver keeps his share (earnings unchanged, Movera pays it: commission = − share); true: an earnings adjustment of − share in the trip currency, earnings 0. A fee carried by a ride going on now → 409 conflict (reason fee_on_running_trip), as for a waive. The reversed no-show no longer counts in the rider's no-show count.
reverseNoShow.idempotent: Again on a reversed trip: 200 with the trip as it is, nothing changes, no second audit row (the first reason stays).

alerts.note: Island messages, no sound (owner decision 6). The server books two timers at arrive: at waiting.freeUntil (paid_waiting_started) and at waiting.noShowAt (no_show_possible). When one fires while the trip is still arrived with the same arrival, waiting.alerts gains { kind, at } and a trip_projection event goes out (no version change, like a search step). Apps show each kind once per trip as a short island message without sound; they may also start it from freeUntil / noShowAt themselves (the event is the server's confirmation). A free wait of 0 min fires paid_waiting_started at arrival.
